Ⅰ. 사무엘상\n 1) 지금으로부터 3 천년 전 이야기\n 2) 내용은:
Ⅰ. 1 Samuel
 1) A story from 3,000 years ago
 2) The content: the story of Samuel's family, the story of Eli's family, the story of Saul, the story of David's young years, and the fall of Saul's royal house.  It's simple.
자~ 다시 한 번 출애굽기 19장 5~6절 구약의 축을 붙잡고 얘기해 봅: All right~ let's hold on once more to the axis of the Old Testament, Exodus 19:5~6, and talk it through. Dreaming of world mission, God chose and took hold of the people of Israel, saved them, gave them the law of the kingdom of God, the Law, sealed it firmly with a promise, and just in case, trained them Himself in the wilderness where nobody could see, and then put them right up on the stage of history. But the lead actor called Israel went up on stage without memorizing a single line of the script and is fumbling around.
그래서 안되겠다. 어려서부터 아예 구별해서 길러가지고 해봐야겠다. 나실인: So, "This won't do. I'll set one apart from childhood and raise him up and try that." He raised up Nazirites, and then the judge goes and falls into corruption too?
아직 사사 시대입니다. 사무엘도 사사예요. 사무엘이 태어난 것도 한나라는: It's still the time of the judges. Samuel is a judge too. Even Samuel's birth: God kept a woman named Hannah from having a child so that she would make a vow. Look at chapter 1, verse 11. "There shall no razor come upon his head"... that's a Nazirite vow, right? And Samuel, born that way, is given to the temple right after he's weaned, just as promised.
And right after that comes the story of Eli's family.
<삼상2:12> 엘리의 아들들은 불량자라 여호와를 알지 아니하더라\n -:
<1 Sam 2:12> Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD.
 - Sons of a priest, and good-for-nothings. They "could not" know the LORD?  No, they "would not" know Him!
<삼상2:17> 이 소년들의 죄가 여호와 앞에 심히 큼은 그들이 여호와의: <1 Sam 2:17> Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD: for men abhorred the offering of the LORD.
제사장의 아들인데 제사를 멸시한다. 귀찮아하는 정도가 아니고 멸시하는 지: Sons of a priest, and they despise the sacrifices. Not just finding it a bother, it got to the point of despising it. So Eli says a word. And still they don't listen. Look at verse 25.
<삼상2:25>그들이 그 아비의 말을 듣지 아니하였으니 이는 여호와께서: <1 Sam 2:25>Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the LORD would slay them.
Seeing they won't listen, looks like He's going to kill them.
<삼상2:29> 너희는 어찌하여 내가 나의 처소에서 명한 나의 제물과 예:
<1 Sam 2:29> Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?
 - Eli's sin was holding his sons more precious than God.
<삼상2:30> 그러므로 이스라엘의 하나님 나 여호와가 말하노라 내가 전:
<1 Sam 2:30> Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
 - We think that once God makes a promise He's stuck keeping it no matter what, but no. He can change it any time, depending on what people do. And we know God only as the God of love, but: those who honor Me I will honor, and if you despise Me, I will despise you too.
Verse 34. Hophni and Phinehas will die on the same day.
<삼상3:13> 내가 그 집을 영영토록 심판하겠다고 그에게 이른 것은 그: <1 Sam 3:13> For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.
A sin he committed knowing full well. And Eli never once said to them, "Don't do that." Raise a kid like that and he turns into a total mess, right? So because of the sin of raising his sons badly, the ark of the LORD ends up being taken by the Philistine army.
그 전쟁에서 홉니와 비느하스가 죽고, 엘리가 그 얘기를 듣다가 의자에서: In that battle Hophni and Phinehas die, Eli hears the news, falls backward off his seat, breaks his neck and dies, and Phinehas's wife, hearing the news, dies giving birth. Because he raised his sons badly, Eli's family is smashed to pieces.
한편 법궤를 가져간 블레셋 재앙이 일어납니다. 법궤를 아스돗으로 가져 갔: Meanwhile, disaster breaks out among the Philistines who took the ark. They carried the ark to Ashdod, and there in Dagon's temple the Philistine idol (Dagon) ends up bowing down to the ark, and the second time with its head and hands cut off. And God struck that region with terrible boils.
그러니까 이 블레셋 사람들이 법궤를 가드로 보내 버립니다. 아니 가드 사: So these Philistines send the ark off to Gath. Hey, what are the people of Gath supposed to do? Terrible boils come on Gath too, so they send the ark to Ekron. So the people of Ekron are in an uproar. No way are we taking it!!
그래서 블레셋 방백들, 장관들이 모여서 말하길, ‘법궤를 돌려 보내자’: So the Philistine lords and officials get together and say, 'Let's send the ark back.'
그래서 제사장들과 복술자들을 불러서 물어보니까 그냥 맨입으로 보내면 안되: So they called the priests and the diviners and asked, and they said you can't send it back empty-handed, you have to send a gift with it, so they make some things out of gold and send them along. What's funny about these people is that even in the middle of all that, they run a test. They make cows that have never once been under a yoke, that have just given birth and haven't even weaned their calves, pull a cart. Cows that have never pulled a cart, and that have calves with them. And these cows go off pulling the cart, lowing all the way, and find the road exactly.
그러는 중에 또 벧세메스 사람들은 ‘이게 뭔가?’ 하고 법궤 안을 들여다: Meanwhile, the people of Beth-shemesh go, 'What's this?' and look inside the ark, and 50,070 of them die. They must have been curious. Cows come along pulling a cart, lowing and lowing, so how curious they must have been.
법궤가 나중에는 기럇여아림의 아비나답 집에서 머무는 이야기가 나오고 미스: Later comes the story of the ark staying in the house of Abinadab in Kiriath-jearim, and the story of Samuel gathering all Israel at Mizpah and praying, and of defeating the Philistines.
<삼상8:1~2> 사무엘이 늙으매 그 아들들로 이스라엘 사사를 삼으니 장: <1 Sam 8:1~2> And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel. Now the name of his firstborn was Joel; and the name of his second, Abiah: they were judges in Beer-sheba.
<삼상8:3> 그 아들들이 그 아비의 행위를 따르지 아니하고 이를 따라서: <1 Sam 8:3> And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.
한 자리 차지하니까 바로 뇌물을 받고 판결을 굽게 해버렸다. 이 사건 때: The moment they got a position, they took bribes and twisted judgment. Because of this incident, God ends up stepping down from the throne.
<삼상8:4~5> 이스라엘 모든 장로가 모여 라마에 있는 사무엘에게 나아: <1 Sam 8:4~5> Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah, and said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.
하나님 보고 권좌에서 물러나라는 얘기죠 이게. 하나님께서는 물러나라고 하: This is basically telling God to step down from the throne. And when told to step down, God simply steps down. So the king they set up is Saul. Israel's first king.
4. 요나단의 용맹\n - 사무엘이 은퇴한 후 사울이 나라를 이끌어 가는:
4. Jonathan's courage
 - After Samuel retires, Saul leads the nation, and at first Saul does all right, but once he gets a taste of power he quickly goes bad. In chapter 13, Samuel is supposed to come but doesn't, he's delayed, so Saul offers the sacrifice himself, which only a priest may do.
그래서 자꾸 사람이 침착하지 못하고 믿음이 없고 점점 흔들리고 약한 면을:
So he keeps showing that he can't stay calm, has no faith, and gets more and more shaky and weak. Jonathan, on the other hand, is a truly outstanding man, a man of courage, a man of faith and nerve.
 - Back then, the Philistines right next door were always the problem, and one day the Philistine army came again and set up camp. So Jonathan took the boy who carried his armor, went into the Philistine camp and attacked the Philistine army. Jonathan didn't even fight much, and they start killing each other with their own swords. Because Jonathan had this kind of faith, when he saw David he liked him so much that he came to love him as his own life.
Saul, on the other hand, keeps making mistakes.
<삼상14:24> 전쟁이 벌어졌는데 금식을 선포해 버린다. 밥을 먹고: <1 Sam 14:24>  A battle breaks out and he declares a fast. Even with a full stomach you might or might not win.... But Jonathan wasn't there when that was said. So as he went along he saw some honey, and being so hungry he dipped his stick in it and licked it, and his eyes lit right up.
근데 이게 또 자기가 한 말이 있으니까 금식 명령을 어기고 꿀을 먹었다고:
But since Saul had said what he said, he orders Jonathan killed for breaking the fast order and eating honey, and the people stop him, and he keeps making mistakes like this.
 - In chapter 15 too, as everyone knows, he was told to utterly destroy Amalek, but he brings back the cattle and sheep and causes grief. And on top of that he makes the excuse that he meant to sacrifice them to God. Like this, King Saul's faith is all doing things his own way, and he listens to God's word half-heartedly at best.
So Samuel comes and says a word.
<삼상15:22~23> 사무엘이 가로되 여호와께서 번제와 다른 제사를 그: <1 Sam 15:22~23> And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
그 유명한 순종이 제사보다 낫다는 말이 여기서 나오네요. 이런 말을 듣고: That famous line, "to obey is better than sacrifice," comes from right here. And even after hearing this, he only thinks about saving face.
<삼상15:30> 사울이 가로되 내가 범죄하였을지라도 청하옵나니 내 백성: <1 Sam 15:30> Then he said, I have sinned: yet honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD thy God.
사람들 앞에서 쪽팔리게 하지 말라는 겁니다. 15장 35절. 이런 사울을: He's saying, don't embarrass me in front of people. Chapter 15, verse 35. Seeing Saul like this, it says God repented that He had made Saul king. And Samuel keeps pleading with God. So God is in an awkward spot.
16장 입니다. 내가 이미 버리기로 작정 했는데 니가 슬퍼하면 어떡하냐?: Chapter 16. I've already decided to reject him, so why are you grieving? Stop talking and hurry off to Jesse. I've prepared another king.
“제사 드리러 왔다고 해”: "Say you came to offer a sacrifice."
그래서 결국 다윗에게 기름을 붓습니다. 기름 붓는 것은 왕이나 주의 종을:
So in the end he anoints David. Anointing carries the meaning of setting apart, when you appoint a king or a servant of the Lord. The Spirit of the LORD comes mightily upon David, but the Spirit of the LORD departs from Saul and an evil spirit troubles him. But look at verse 14. Who sends that evil spirit? God sends it. And so Saul is on the way down. Later the woman with a familiar spirit at Endor shows up, and that woman, a medium, pretends to be Samuel and toys with King Saul.
 - Chapter 17 has the story of Goliath. It's a famous story, so I won't say more about it.
 - When David tells the story of guarding his flock, it's really something. He basically already had what it takes to be a shepherd. He says he fought a lion and a bear and won, but you can't beat those with your bare hands, right?
다윗은 물매돌 선수라. 이런게 물매라는건데: David was an ace with the sling. This is what a sling is.
한 쪽은 고리가 있죠? 그 고리를 손가락에 걸고: One end has a loop, right? You hook that loop on your finger
이렇게 빙빙 돌리다가 한쪽을 놔버리면 돌이 무시무시한 속도로 날아가는 거: and swing it round and round like this, and when you let go of one end, the stone flies off at a frightening speed. One end is still hooked on your finger, so only the stone shoots out.  It's more powerful than a pistol.
골리앗의 이마를 우연히 맞춘게 아니다. 평소에 자기 양 떼를 지키려고 물: He didn't hit Goliath's forehead by chance. He had practiced with the sling a huge amount, normally, to protect his flock. To guard his sheep. And unless you're pretty confident, you don't go after a lion or a bear.
후에 다윗이 자기 군대를 양성할 때 물매나 활 쏘는 사람들은 오른손, 왼: Later, when David trained his own army, he had the slingers and archers practice with both right hand and left hand. An ambidextrous army is frightening. Tactically, too.
골리앗을 이긴 것까지는 좋았는데 그것 때문에 다윗은 오히려 사울에게 미움: Beating Goliath was great, but because of it David ends up hated by Saul instead. Saul is a lump of jealousy and can't stand anyone better than himself.
또 여자들이 다윗은 만만이요 사울은 천천이다 하면서 사울의 자존심을 상하: And the women go, "David has slain his ten thousands, Saul his thousands," hurting Saul's pride... Saul was jealous already, and with the crowd lifting David higher, Saul completely loses it.
그 길로 다윗은 사울을 피해 도망 다니는 인생을 살게 됩니다. 그러면서도: From then on David lives a life of running away from Saul. And through it all he himself never kills Saul.  Saul throws a spear to kill him, and lures him with the promise of his daughter Merab and drives him off to war.
<삼상18:17> 사울이 다윗에게 이르되 내 맏딸 메랍을 네게 아내로 주: <1 Sam 18:17> And Saul said to David, Behold my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight the LORD's battles. For Saul said, Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.
이 나쁜 놈이 꼴에 또 자기 손 더럽히기는 싫다는 겁니다. 그리고 메랍을: This rotten guy, of all things, doesn't want to get his own hands dirty. And after saying he'd give Merab, he gives her away to someone else and then puts Michal up as the prize. Reminds you of Laban, doesn't it?
블레셋 사람 양피 일백을 가져오면 주겠다 함. 양피라는게 남자 생식기인데: He says he'll give her if David brings a hundred Philistine foreskins. A foreskin is part of a man's private parts, you can't borrow those, so he'd have no choice but to kill 100 Philistine men and cut them off, and doing something that repulsive he'd probably get caught and killed. That's the trick.
눈치 없는 다윗이 200개를 잘라 옵니다. 그리고 미갈이 다윗을 사랑하는:
David, not catching on, cuts off 200 and brings them. And when Saul sees that Michal loves David, he fears David more and more.
 - In chapter 20, Jonathan sees that David is in danger, so he makes an agreement with David. I'll sound out my father one last time. Jonathan checks, and there's no hope. So in the end David and Jonathan part ways.
21장 입니다. 다윗이 놉으로 가서 진설병을 얻어먹고 가드로 갑니다. 원: Chapter 21. David goes to Nob, gets the showbread to eat, and goes to Gath. Normally only the priests can eat the showbread, but life comes first, so he ate it. When he gets to Gath, look at verses 10 and 11. "Is not this David the king of the land?" David is already a king.
그래서 다윗이 순발력 있게 미친놈 연기를 합니다. 침을 흘리고 대문짝에: So David thinks fast and acts like a madman. Drooling and rubbing himself against the doors of the gate... and barely gets away.
22장 입니다. 다윗은 아둘람 굴로 도망을 갔는데 그 형제와 아비의 식구: Chapter 22. David fled to the cave of Adullam, and his brothers and all his father's household, everyone in distress, everyone in debt, everyone bitter of soul, people juggling credit cards, people in personal bankruptcy... about 400 people gathered like this. Counting kids and women, easily 1,000. So imagine how hard it was for David, on the run himself, to be responsible for 1,000 people.
어쩔 수 없이 모압으로 갑니다. 모압 왕에게 망명을 요청해서 살고 있었더: With no other choice he goes to Moab. He asks the king of Moab for asylum and lives there, and then God tells him to leave and go to the land of Judah. At that time, in chapter 22, Saul, together with Doeg the Edomite, kills Ahimelech, the priest of Nob who had given David a sword and bread, and the other 80 priests, every one of them.  Only one man, Abiathar, barely escapes and goes to David.
<삼상23:1> 혹이 다윗에게 고하여 가로되 보소서 블레셋 사람이 그일라: <1 Sam 23:1> Then they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines fight against Keilah, and they rob the threshingfloors.
- 그렇게 살면서도 또 유다땅이 위험하면 가서 구원해 주곤 합니다. 속도:
- Even living like that, whenever the land of Judah is in danger he goes and rescues it. Does he have no resentment at all...
 - If you trace David's escape route: Gibeah -> Ramah -> Nob -> Gath -> Mizpeh of Moab -> forest of Hereth -> Keilah -> wilderness of Ziph -> hill of Hachilah -> wilderness of Maon -> En-gedi -> Gath -> Ziklag -> Hebron -> Jerusalem, and like this he was chased around for about 10 years
 - To catch this David, Saul sends out three thousand men at a time to follow him, but David can always see Saul while Saul can never see David. And at the decisive moment when he's about to catch him, a war breaks out and he has to turn back, again and again, so he never catches David.
.
 - Even when things were this hard, David had his principles.
<삼상26:9~10> 다윗이 아비새에게 이르되 죽이지 말라 누구든지 손을:
<1 Sam 26:9~10> And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the LORD's anointed, and be guiltless? David said furthermore, As the LORD liveth, the LORD shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
 - I will not lift my hand against the anointed one. He's quietly telling the people around him something. I'm anointed too.
 - While David was going through these hard times, there was a man named Nabal around Maon. David had been camped there and protected their flocks, so at sheep-shearing time David asks for help. Not asking for a lot, just, you've come to a good day, so help us out a little.
근데 이 나발이 다윗을 진 나온 노예 취급을 하면서 일언지하에 거절을 하: But this Nabal treats David like a runaway slave and flatly refuses.'What? Every man of you, strap on your sword. We'll go kill him, and I'll pay what a dog is worth.'
나발의 아내 아비가일이 이 소식을 듣고 지혜로운 말로 다윗의 화를 풀어주: Nabal's wife Abigail hears the news and calms David's anger with wise words, and her words were smooth as sesame oil. She spoke so beautifully and so well that David's heart softened and he went back.
디질뻔 했다는 말을 들은 나발은 몸이 돌덩이처럼 굳어서 죽어 버려요. 다:
Nabal, hearing that he nearly got himself killed, goes stiff as a stone and dies. David right away proposes to Abigail. Abigail is not a young girl, she's an old woman. An old woman. How hard up David must have been to propose to an old widow. A rich widow.
 - Meanwhile Saul keeps making mistakes, and ends up dying in battle against the Philistines.
<삼상31:1~6> 블레셋 사람이 이스라엘을 치매 이스라엘 사람들이 블레:
<1 Sam 31:1~6> Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul's sons. And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers. Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him. So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.
 - After that, the men of Jabesh-gilead go up, bring back Saul's body and bury him, and that's how 1 Samuel wraps up.
